tasks.title: Create the installable Ralph CLI entrypoint
tasks.objective: Add the Python package scaffold and `ralph run <path>` command surface that becomes the stable public entrypoint for the harness.
out_of_scope: Do not implement lifecycle looping or step execution logic in this task.
Do not modify `backend/pyproject.toml` or backend packaging.
Do not keep any retrospective-only CLI mode in the new Python interface.
existing_context: The repository currently exposes Ralph only through `ralph/ralph.sh`.
The spec requires the stable public command shape `ralph run <path>`.
The glossary in `ralph/CONTEXT.md` defines the CLI as the owner of command parsing and exit-code mapping.
constraints: The primary public entrypoint must be `ralph run <path>` rather than legacy flag-only invocation.
Parse `--agent`, `--model`, `--max-iterations`, and `--log` on the `run` subcommand and pass them into the run context unchanged.
Expose defaults of `codex` for `--agent` and `gpt-5.4` for `--model` at the CLI layer.
Keep the CLI package rooted under `ralph/` while using a repository-root package manifest to expose the console script.
implementation_guidelines: Create a repository-root `pyproject.toml` that installs a console-script entrypoint named `ralph` and points it at the Python CLI main function.
Implement `ralph/__main__.py` so `python -m ralph` and the console script share the same execution path.
Model the `run` subcommand as a thin adapter that validates command-line syntax and forwards typed values to the orchestrator layer.
Keep help text and argument names aligned with the spec wording so later wrapper delegation is mechanical.
acceptance_criteria: The repository contains a Python package entrypoint that exposes `ralph run <path>` through both `python -m ralph` and a console-script definition.
The `run` subcommand help text documents `--agent`, `--model`, `--max-iterations`, and `--log`.
The CLI layer defines `codex` as the default agent and `gpt-5.4` as the default model when the user omits both flags.
No lifecycle loop, prompt execution, or shell-wrapper compatibility logic is implemented inside `ralph/cli.py`.
assumptions: Adding a repository-root `pyproject.toml` for the Ralph package is acceptable even though the backend already has its own `backend/pyproject.toml`.
A dedicated retrospective command is intentionally excluded from the MVP because the spec limits the public CLI to `run` mode.

tasks.title: Define immutable run and lifecycle contracts
tasks.objective: Introduce the shared typed contracts that let the CLI, orchestrator, workflow steps, and agents interact without hidden mutable state.
out_of_scope: Do not implement the Code step prompt flow in this task.
Do not execute any agent process in this task.
Do not wire shell-wrapper argument translation in this task.
existing_context: The spec defines `Step`, `Step result`, and `Run context` as the core lifecycle contracts.
The glossary in `ralph/CONTEXT.md` requires the run context to be immutable and to include a stable run identifier.
The spec requires deterministic exit outcomes for success, blocked, failure, and invalid usage or setup errors.
constraints: The only valid step outcomes are `repeat`, `complete`, `blocked`, and `fail`.
The run context must be immutable after creation and must include the feature directory, selected agent, selected model, max-iterations limit, and stable `run_id`.
Exit outcomes must be representable without inspecting workflow artifact contents.
Keep lifecycle contracts independent of any specific agent implementation.
implementation_guidelines: Define typed data structures for step results, run outcomes, and the immutable run context before implementing orchestration behavior.
Keep the run identifier generation contract inside the orchestrator-facing types so observability and tests can rely on one source of truth.
Represent blocked and failed terminal states separately so the CLI can map them to distinct exit codes later.
Document any serialization-facing fields that will be reused by the JSONL logger.
acceptance_criteria: The lifecycle module exposes a structured step-result type whose allowed outcomes are limited to `repeat`, `complete`, `blocked`, and `fail`.
The orchestrator-facing run-context type is immutable and includes a stable `run_id` plus all shared run inputs named in the spec.
The codebase contains a distinct representation for successful completion, blocked termination, failed termination, and usage or setup errors.
No lifecycle contract type depends on a concrete Codex command line or prompt file path.
assumptions: The optional `--log` destination can live on the run context as nullable metadata because it does not violate run-context immutability.
A deterministic iteration-cap termination will be modeled as a failure outcome rather than a blocked outcome.

tasks.title: Implement the built-in agent registry and Codex runner
tasks.objective: Add the built-in agent abstraction and the MVP `codex` implementation that performs one AFK prompt invocation per request.
out_of_scope: Do not add support for runtime-discovered or user-defined agents.
Do not implement orchestration retry logic in this task.
Do not parse the Code step JSON contract in this task.
existing_context: The current shell script invokes Codex directly with non-interactive approval flags.
The spec fixes the built-in agent registry to static names and declares `codex` as the default.
The glossary in `ralph/CONTEXT.md` distinguishes agent execution from workflow-step logic.
constraints: Agent lookup must be by built-in name and must fail fast for unknown names.
Each agent execution must issue exactly one prompt invocation and return exactly one structured agent result.
The Codex implementation must run in AFK mode without interactive approval prompts.
The selected model must be passed through from the run context without the workflow layer renaming it.
implementation_guidelines: Define an agent interface that accepts the prompt payload plus typed run metadata and returns a structured result with raw stdout or response text.
Centralize the built-in registry so the CLI or orchestrator can validate the requested agent name without hard-coding `codex` in multiple places.
Carry enough process metadata in the agent result to distinguish successful execution from transport or subprocess failure.
Mirror the current shell harness AFK behavior instead of inventing any approval or sandbox configuration knobs.
acceptance_criteria: The agents module exposes a built-in registry that resolves `codex` and rejects unknown names before workflow execution continues.
The Codex agent implementation performs a single non-interactive invocation per request and accepts the caller-selected model value.
Agent execution returns a structured result that preserves the raw response text for later parsing and logging.
No user-configurable agent plugin or discovery mechanism is introduced.
assumptions: The MVP can continue using the existing Codex AFK execution style as the behavioral baseline for the first built-in agent.
Subprocess-level failures from Codex should surface as failed agent results rather than thrown uncaught exceptions.

tasks.title: Implement the single-iteration Code step contract
tasks.objective: Build the Code step so it loads the built-in prompt, invokes the selected agent once, and converts only strict JSON responses into step results.
out_of_scope: Do not add any retrospective step or follow-up workflow step.
Do not let the orchestrator inspect `tasks.json` directly in this task.
Do not let the harness write or normalize `ralph.txt` contents in this task.
existing_context: The existing prompt template already lives at `ralph/prompts/code.md`.
The spec assigns task selection and prompt construction to the Code step, not to the orchestrator.
The glossary in `ralph/CONTEXT.md` defines the Code step as exactly one coding iteration.
constraints: The Code step must perform exactly one agent invocation per execution.
Only a JSON-only agent response may be parsed successfully; surrounding prose or malformed content must be rejected.
The converted step result may expose only `repeat`, `complete`, `blocked`, or `fail` outcomes.
Prompt handling must keep workflow artifacts such as `ralph.txt` model-managed rather than harness-managed.
implementation_guidelines: Load the checked-in code-step prompt template from `ralph/prompts/code.md` and substitute the feature-directory input without re-embedding the prompt text in Python.
Treat any agent subprocess failure as a `fail` step result with a concise failure summary and preserved raw response metadata.
Validate the entire returned payload as JSON rather than scanning for a sentinel line or parsing partial text.
Convert valid JSON responses into typed step results and reject any unexpected status value or missing required field.
acceptance_criteria: Executing the Code step reads the checked-in prompt template and issues exactly one agent call.
A JSON payload that matches the step contract is converted into a structured step result with one of the four allowed outcomes.
A response that includes extra prose, malformed JSON, or an unknown outcome is rejected as a failed step result.
The harness-side Code step code does not create, truncate, or rewrite `ralph.txt`.
assumptions: Leading and trailing whitespace around an otherwise valid JSON document may be trimmed before validation, but any non-whitespace wrapper text must be rejected.
If prompt-template edits are required, they should be limited to placeholder compatibility with the new Python step implementation.

tasks.title: Implement the hard-coded run orchestrator
tasks.objective: Add the Ralph lifecycle orchestrator that validates required artifacts, runs the Code step loop, and terminates with deterministic outcomes.
out_of_scope: Do not add runtime-configurable workflow composition or additional step types.
Do not inspect or validate the internal contents of `spec.md` or `tasks.json` beyond required-file existence.
Do not add retrospective execution paths.
existing_context: The spec hard-codes a single-step MVP workflow whose only step id is `code`.
The current shell script already validates feature-directory existence and required files before execution.
The glossary in `ralph/CONTEXT.md` states that workflow transitions belong only to the orchestrator.
constraints: The orchestrator must validate that the feature directory exists and contains `spec.md` and `tasks.json` before invoking any step.
A `repeat` step result reruns the last executed step, which is the Code step in the MVP.
A `complete` result ends the run successfully when no follow-up step exists.
A `blocked` result must print the blocker text exactly as returned, and a `fail` result must print the failure summary with a failure exit outcome.
implementation_guidelines: Keep the MVP transition table explicit in code instead of deriving it from configuration or workflow artifacts.
Track iterations in the orchestrator so `--max-iterations` is enforced independently of the Code step prompt.
Return typed run outcomes to the CLI rather than calling `sys.exit()` from deep inside the orchestrator.
Handle the iteration cap as a deterministic terminal failure with a human-readable summary.
acceptance_criteria: Starting a run against a missing directory or a directory missing `spec.md` or `tasks.json` stops before any agent invocation.
A `repeat` Code-step result causes the orchestrator to rerun the Code step until a non-repeat terminal outcome or the iteration cap is reached.
A `complete` result from the Code step ends the run successfully because no follow-up step exists in the MVP.
Blocked, failed, and iteration-cap terminations are distinguishable from successful completion through deterministic run outcomes and CLI exit-code mapping.
assumptions: Reaching the iteration cap is treated as a failed termination rather than a blocked termination because the spec only reserves blocked for agent-supplied unblock text.
Setup errors such as a missing feature directory will use the invalid usage or setup exit path rather than the workflow failure path.

tasks.title: Add terminal progress output and JSONL event logging
tasks.objective: Implement the always-on human-readable run reporting and the optional stable JSONL event stream for machine consumers.
out_of_scope: Do not make machine-readable logging enabled by default.
Do not mutate workflow artifacts such as `ralph.txt` to store run events.
Do not change the step-result contract to accommodate logging-only fields.
existing_context: The shell harness currently prints human-readable progress directly from Bash.
The spec requires console output on every run and JSONL only when `--log <path>` is provided.
The stable `run_id` introduced on the run context must appear in every event record.
constraints: Human-readable terminal progress is always enabled even when JSONL logging is disabled.
The JSONL event schema must remain stable and must emit at least `run_started`, `step_started`, `agent_invoked`, `step_finished`, and `run_finished`.
Every JSONL record must include the stable `run_id` plus timestamp and relevant step or agent context.
When a step fails because an agent response cannot be parsed or validated, the JSONL stream must preserve the raw failed agent response.
implementation_guidelines: Keep the event-writer implementation separate from the terminal presenter so tests can assert the JSONL contract without parsing ANSI text.
Emit events from the orchestrator and step boundaries instead of from the shell wrapper.
Attach the raw agent response only on failure paths that need debugging evidence rather than on every successful event.
Open the JSONL file only when `--log` is set and append one valid JSON object per line.
acceptance_criteria: A normal run prints clear terminal messages for run start, step progress, agent usage, and final outcome even when `--log` is omitted.
A run started with `--log <path>` writes newline-delimited JSON objects whose event types include the five required schema events.
Every emitted JSONL record contains the stable `run_id` from the immutable run context.
If agent output cannot be parsed or validated, the resulting failure event includes the raw agent response for debugging.
assumptions: Creating parent directories for the requested log path is not required unless the chosen file-writing utility already does so naturally.
A stable JSONL schema can be documented by field names in code and README text without generating a separate JSON Schema file.

tasks.title: Reduce the shell entrypoint to a compatibility wrapper
tasks.objective: Replace the legacy Bash lifecycle implementation with a thin wrapper that delegates supported legacy arguments to the new Python CLI.
out_of_scope: Do not preserve the Bash implementation loop, prompt execution, or retrospective flow.
Do not add new shell-only behavior that differs from the Python CLI.
Do not reimplement JSON parsing or status handling in Bash.
existing_context: The current `ralph/ralph.sh` owns argument parsing, feature validation, Codex execution, loop control, and retrospective behavior.
The spec keeps `ralph/ralph.sh` only as a temporary migration wrapper.
The legacy wrapper currently accepts `--feature-dir`, `--max-iterations`, `--coding-model`, `--retro-model`, and `--retro-only`.
constraints: The wrapper must delegate supported lifecycle arguments to the Python CLI instead of owning any independent workflow logic.
Legacy `--feature-dir` must map to the new positional `<path>` argument, and `--coding-model` must map to `--model`.
Unsupported legacy retrospective flags must fail fast with an explicit migration error instead of silently pretending the Python CLI still supports them.
Keep the wrapper narrow enough that future removal is a file deletion, not another migration project.
implementation_guidelines: Strip the script down to argument translation, Python CLI invocation, and minimal usage or migration messaging.
Use one execution path that eventually runs the new Python CLI rather than leaving fallback shell logic behind.
Translate only the legacy arguments that map directly onto the MVP `run` mode.
Return the Python CLI exit code unchanged so the wrapper does not invent a second exit-code contract.
acceptance_criteria: The shell wrapper no longer contains Codex subprocess invocation, prompt-file loading, iteration looping, or retrospective execution logic.
Invoking `ralph/ralph.sh` with supported legacy run arguments delegates to the Python CLI behavior instead of a Bash lifecycle implementation.
Passing unsupported legacy retrospective flags fails fast with a clear migration message and a non-zero exit status.
The wrapper preserves the Python CLI exit status without remapping successful, blocked, failed, or setup-error outcomes.
assumptions: Because the MVP only covers `run`, the compatibility wrapper may reject `--retro-only` and `--retro-model` instead of emulating the retired retrospective flow.
The wrapper may invoke `python -m ralph` directly from the repository checkout even though the installed console script name is also `ralph`.

tasks.title: Document the CLI contract and JSONL schema
tasks.objective: Update Ralph’s public documentation so the new CLI surface, exit behavior, and machine-readable event schema are explicit and stable.
out_of_scope: Do not edit `docs/plans/ralph-cli/*` or restore obsolete retrospective design material.
Do not rewrite the Ralph feature spec in `docs/plans/ralph-harness/spec.md`.
Do not add installation instructions for unrelated backend or extension tooling.
existing_context: The current `ralph/README.md` still documents the Bash harness and retrospective-only mode.
The current `ralph/CONTEXT.md` already defines the domain terms introduced by the harness spec.
The spec treats the JSONL schema as a stable public contract rather than an internal debugging detail.
constraints: Document `ralph run <path>` as the primary public entrypoint and remove or clearly retire obsolete retrospective-only usage.
List the supported run flags and their defaults exactly as implemented by the Python CLI.
Describe the JSONL event schema in terms of required event types and required shared fields such as `run_id` and timestamp.
Document deterministic exit behavior for success, blocked termination, failed termination, and invalid usage or setup errors.
implementation_guidelines: Rewrite the usage section around the Python CLI first, then explain the temporary shell wrapper as migration-only compatibility behavior.
Keep `ralph/CONTEXT.md` aligned with any concrete field names or module names introduced by the implementation so the glossary stays authoritative.
Document the JSONL schema in a way that downstream automation can rely on without reading the code.
Remove references to the obsolete retrospective lifecycle from user-facing documentation unless they are explicitly described as retired migration history.
acceptance_criteria: `ralph/README.md` documents `ralph run <path>` as the primary entrypoint and names the supported `run` flags with their defaults.
`ralph/README.md` describes the JSONL logging contract, including the required event types and the shared `run_id` field.
`ralph/README.md` states the deterministic exit-behavior categories for success, blocked, failed, and invalid usage or setup errors.
`ralph/CONTEXT.md` remains consistent with the implemented module boundaries and does not describe the old Bash harness as the canonical architecture.
assumptions: The public JSONL schema can be documented directly in `ralph/README.md` without creating a separate schema artifact.
Keeping the glossary current in `ralph/CONTEXT.md` is sufficient for module-boundary documentation in this repo.

tasks.title: Add automated verification for the Ralph harness MVP
tasks.objective: Create the focused automated test coverage that proves the new CLI, orchestrator, step parsing, logging, and wrapper behaviors match the MVP contract.
out_of_scope: Do not add live Codex-dependent integration tests that require networked or attended runs.
Do not broaden the test suite into retrospective or multi-step workflow scenarios that the MVP excludes.
Do not modify obsolete `docs/plans/ralph-cli/*` fixtures or plans.
existing_context: The repository does not currently contain a dedicated Ralph Python test suite.
The spec’s edge cases enumerate the invalid-path, missing-artifact, unknown-agent, malformed-response, blocked, complete, and iteration-cap scenarios that must be covered.
The shell wrapper is temporary, so its tests should focus on delegation and rejection behavior rather than re-testing workflow internals.
constraints: Tests must stub or fake agent execution so the suite is deterministic and does not require real Codex runs.
Validation coverage must include CLI defaults and option handling, strict JSON-only parsing, orchestrator transition rules, JSONL event emission, and wrapper delegation.
The validation task must verify the exact blocked-message passthrough requirement and the presence of raw failed agent responses in JSONL failure paths.
Keep test execution local and automation-friendly by using a standard Python test runner from the repository checkout.
implementation_guidelines: Add focused unit tests for each module boundary instead of one monolithic end-to-end test file.
Use temporary directories and fake feature folders to verify required-artifact validation and optional log-file output.
Mock the agent registry and agent execution boundaries so transition behavior is tested independently of the Codex subprocess implementation.
Include wrapper tests that assert supported legacy arguments are translated correctly and unsupported retrospective flags fail fast.
acceptance_criteria: The Ralph test suite covers CLI defaulting and flag parsing, unknown-agent rejection, missing feature artifacts, repeat or complete or blocked or fail orchestrator outcomes, strict JSON-only parsing, and iteration-cap termination.
The logging tests verify that `run_started`, `step_started`, `agent_invoked`, `step_finished`, and `run_finished` events are emitted with a stable `run_id` in every record when `--log` is enabled.
The failure-path logging tests verify that an unparseable or invalid agent response is preserved in the machine-readable log.
Running `python -m unittest discover -s ralph/tests` from the repository root succeeds without requiring a real Codex invocation.
assumptions: Using the standard library `unittest` runner is acceptable for the new Ralph package because the repository does not currently define a root-level pytest dependency.
Wrapper-behavior tests may execute the shell script through subprocesses that stub the Python CLI target instead of invoking the full installed console script.
